craft_claim: Irreverence derives its charge from collapsing a status or sanctity gap in the moment — the elevated register is made to stand at the audience's level — rather than from arguing against it.

supporting_evidence.note: The carnival frame temporarily inverts rank, bringing the lofty down for a defined duration before ordinary hierarchy resumes.
Kyōgen stages a servant defying a master and an arrogant authority figure made ridiculous, inside the sanctioned slot of the nō program — status collapse performed, not argued.
The article's framing positions the folk figure Nasreddin as the humorous antagonist of the powerful Timur — a documented non-Anglophone tradition of teasing the mighty.

supporting_evidence.location: Introduction p. xvi; Poem XXI pp. 28-29; Poems LXV-LXVII pp. 68-71; Poem LXIX pp. 72-73
supporting_evidence.note: Kabir's verses drag priestly costume, ritual bath, rosary, and idol down to the level of seen-through performance — the sanctity gap collapsed through ridicule rather than refutation.

supporting_evidence.location: Frame verified via Project Gutenberg ebook #2400 record; tales not inspected
supporting_evidence.note: The riddle-cycle frame licenses a reanimated corpse's repeated impertinence toward a sovereign — a structural device for leveling royal omniscience (frame-level support only; analysis_status partial).

counterevidence.note: Hobbes's 'sudden glory' account makes laughter an assertion of superiority over its object — mockery can ENACT rank rather than level it, so the same deflation can be read as putting the target down instead of bringing them across.
Norm-violating humor lowers the speaker's own status in the audience's eyes — leveling attempts can backfire into status loss for the leveller when the frame is wrong.

scope: Momentary status collapse of an elevated register (office, ceremony, sanctity, self-importance) inside a comic frame; it is a claim about the reader's felt experience of the moment, not about political outcomes.
exceptions: No evidence reviewed shows that literary deflation changes power relations; claims of real-world leveling would be evidence-incomplete.
When the leveller is perceived as punching down, the mechanism inverts into hierarchy enforcement (see clm-tone-irreverent-prejudiced-norm-backfire).
